title: College Type Sorter
creator: Beth Kullberg
subject: College Admissions
description: A drag-and-drop sorting activity: classify twelve real colleges as public or private and as a research university or liberal arts college, then decide which public research universities are flagships.

learningObjectives: Students will classify a four-year college as public or private and as a research university or liberal arts college, and explain the clue in its description that decides each label.
prerequisites: Chapter 1: The College Landscape and Application Rounds

controls: State funded / Many graduate programs / Mainly undergraduates checkboxes

keyQuestions: Why is every flagship a public research university, but not every public research university a flagship?
Which clue in a profile tells you a school is public?
Why might a public liberal arts college be rare?
commonMisconceptions: A school called a 'College' must be small or undergraduate-only (Dartmouth College is a research university).
Every big public university is the state's flagship (Iowa State is not).
assessmentOpportunities: Students sort at least ten of twelve cards correctly on the first try and can name the deciding clue for any card.
